operations_plan.summary: Establish the axial orientation and dimensional parameters for the edit. Identify the existing side with the 10 mm outer rounded return as the requested top, making the opposite broad planar annular face the bottom support plane.

steps.description: Identify the continuous large-radius outer edge treatment represented by the 10 mm-radius rear outer rounded return. This return is feature_03_03 on faces 35 through 42 and is adjacent to the narrow rear annular land on face 34. Designate this -Z/rear side as the requested top without modifying it.

Designate the opposite +Z/front side, represented primarily by the broad planar annular seating face 12, as the bottom. Use the plane of face 12 as the bottom datum for the new support. Define the support-growth direction as inward through the part thickness toward the designated top, nominally in the -Z direction.

Normalize the requested dimensions to model units: inner-wall offset equals 20 mm, support axial thickness equals 5 mm, and upper-edge blend radius equals 2 mm. Interpret the 20 mm offset as projection from the existing inner wall into the central opening, since this creates the requested wider bottom bearing area while preserving the external footprint.

operations_plan.summary: Create a new continuous bottom support section by offsetting the existing rounded-rectangular inner-wall profile 20 mm into the opening and additively extruding the resulting annular region 5 mm toward the top.

steps.description: Create a sketch on the bottom datum plane coincident with broad annular face 12. Project or derive the nominal rounded-rectangular footprint of the existing inner opening wall from its four planar wall faces and four 50 mm-radius cylindrical corner faces. Use the wall's virtual tangent profile rather than the boundary of the existing 2 mm bottom fillet so that the support joins the true inner-wall envelope continuously around the frame.

Use the projected existing inner-wall profile as the outer boundary of the support ledge. Offset this complete profile by 20 mm toward the center of the opening to create the new lower aperture boundary. Maintain a closed, concentric rounded-rectangular loop with straight segments parallel to the existing opening. For an exact geometric offset of the existing 50 mm corner radius, the new aperture corner radius becomes 30 mm. Confirm that the offset does not self-intersect and that a continuous annular sketch region exists.

Additively extrude the closed annular support region by 5 mm from the bottom datum toward the designated top (-Z). Keep the support underside exactly coincident and coplanar with face 12. Ensure the support's outer sketch boundary contacts or slightly overlaps the existing frame material at the inner wall so the extrusion fuses robustly with solid 0 rather than creating a separate body. The support must occupy only the central-opening side of the inner wall and must not change the existing outer perimeter.

Boolean-union the support extrusion with solid 0 and heal coincident geometry. Merge the coplanar underside of the support with the existing broad bottom seating face where possible, producing one enlarged, continuous, flat bottom-bearing surface. Confirm that the original inner opening remains unchanged above the 5 mm-high support and that the resulting model remains one continuous solid.

operations_plan.summary: Apply 2 mm blends only to the top-side edges of the newly created support, while retaining sharp lower support edges and a planar underside.

steps.description: After the union, identify the new top-facing annular surface located 5 mm from the bottom datum. Select its continuous outer junction edge where the support meets the existing inner opening wall. This edge is generated by the support operation and is therefore resolved topologically from the intersection of the new top face and the preserved inner-wall faces.

Apply a continuous 2 mm-radius fillet to the upper outer junction edge of the support, blending the support's top surface smoothly into the existing inner wall above. Propagate the fillet around all straight and rounded portions of the inner perimeter. Do not modify the existing inner-wall geometry above the blend termination.

Identify the continuous upper inner edge of the support surrounding the new reduced lower opening and apply a 2 mm-radius fillet to it, creating a smooth approach from above to the support ledge. Keep this fillet entirely on the upper side of the support and verify that it fits within the 5 mm support thickness. This step follows the interpretation that all newly created top-side support edges receive the specified radius.

Explicitly exclude every edge incident to the new bottom support face from filleting, especially the lower inner rounded-rectangular aperture edge. Preserve the support underside as a planar surface coincident with the original bottom datum and retain sharp, well-defined lower step edges. Do not remove or alter pre-existing frame edge treatments outside the newly added support, including the 10 mm top return and existing 2 mm frame fillets.

Validate the final topology and dimensions: one solid; unchanged external rounded-rectangular footprint; 20 mm inward support projection; 5 mm support height from the flat bottom; 2 mm radii only on the new support's upper edges; no radii on its lower edges; preserved larger-radius top return; and an unchanged original opening profile above the support.
